question: Should OpenClaw add a default-off `tools.exec.pty` config default for non-sandbox exec, or keep PTY as a per-call-only tool parameter?
rationale: The missing behavior is source-reproducible, but the fix adds a new global shell-exec default that changes operator-controlled PTY behavior across approval and sandbox boundaries.

options.title: Approve Narrow Config Default
options.body: Add `tools.exec.pty` as an optional false-by-default setting with per-call override precedence, gateway approval coverage, docs, and sandbox behavior tests.

options.title: Keep Per-Call Only
options.body: Avoid another exec config knob and improve docs or skill guidance for commands that require PTY.

options.title: Defer For PTY Policy Review
options.body: Hold this until maintainers settle the broader PTY default and sandbox-warning behavior with the related sandbox issue.

recommendation.title: Approve Narrow Config Default
recommendation.body: Add `tools.exec.pty` as an optional false-by-default setting with per-call override precedence, gateway approval coverage, docs, and sandbox behavior tests.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle introduced the existing exec PTY support and is the strongest history-backed decision owner for changing its defaulting contract.
